why: The statement asks for completeness of Ω-logic (Ω-validity implies Ω-provability) for all sentences. The 1985 result and the 2009 Koellner–Woodin paper concern Ω-completeness of a theory (ZFC + CH deciding every Σ²₁ sentence) and the uniqueness of such theories. That is a different property from the completeness of the logic, so I scored both as variant and not case. It was the closest call: one could read a Σ²₁ completeness instance as a fragment, but the record's own description is about theories deciding sentences, not about valid sentences being provable. Goldberg–Hathaway (May 2025) is the only event after the snapshot. Its Ω-results either assume the conjecture or restate it as an equivalent schema (Prop 8.6), and its unconditional absoluteness theorem is a different question. A reformulation or a conditional transfer settles and bounds nothing, so scope is none. The 2011 chapter, Meadows, the CBH refutation and Sanchez do not address the conjecture's truth. No AI system appears in any event.
doubts: The unverified Dehornoy 'proved for a large fragment' lead comes from a search summary of unreadable slides, has no date, and is contradicted by the same author's 2026 encyclopedia article. It is not an event in the record and I did not score it. If it is real, it would be a pre-snapshot or undated case.
